headline: Graph, ODE and mediation models integrate proteomic and transcriptomic patient data
label: Multiomics Statistical Modeling Frameworks
summary: Proteogenomic datasets from CPTAC and TCGA now support graph, mediation and digital-twin models linking multi-omic layers to outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit biological or statistical structure imposed on multi-omic measurements. PathMoG organizes features into KEGG pathway modules within a graph neural network with dual attention for survival prediction across 10 TCGA cancers, with interpretability. bioGraph applies biologically informed heterogeneous graph learning to infer proteo-transcriptomic networks, and SMAHP uses accelerated failure time models for survival mediation analysis of high-dimensional proteogenomic data. A proteome-calibrated ODE model of the glioblastoma astrocyte, fitted to CPTAC patient proteomics, extends this toward mechanistic simulation of EGFRvIII and PTEN perturbations. MultiOmicsXplorer provides an R Shiny interface for browsing and protein activity inference on CPTAC data. The set is heterogeneous, and the items do not share a single modeling approach; what they share is an effort to encode known pathway, network, or causal organization directly into the analysis of patient multi-omic data.
